enrich_summary.reasoning_short: The top enriched terms are mostly generic metabolic pathways (e.g., energy metabolism hsa00920, cofactor metabolism hsa00130) and viral processing/replication (hsa03265, hsa03450), which are not cell-type specific. The marker list contains TP63 (basal epithelial master regulator), KRTAP19-8 (keratin-associated protein), PKP1 and DSC1 (desmosomal proteins, typical of stratified squamous epithelia), CDH3 (P-cadherin, basal epithelial), FGFR3 (basal/proliferative airway), and FERMT1 (kindlin-1, expressed in basal keratinocytes). Notably, there is no CD3D/CD3E/CD8A (T cell), no CD68/LYZ (macrophage), and no SFTPC/AGER (alveolar). The presence of FGFBP2 is typically NK/T-cell related, but here it is likely a contamination/out-of-scope signal as no other NK/T markers are present. The pathways reflect proliferative/metabolic activity, consistent with basal cell activation. Thus, the core identity is basal epithelial, with possible squamous differentiation markers (PKP1, DSC1, KRTAP19-8).

The presence of FGFBP2 is typically NK/T-cell related, but here it is likely a contamination/out-of-scope signal as no other NK/T markers are present. The pathways reflect proliferative/metabolic activity, consistent with basal cell activation. Thus, the core identity is basal epithelial, with possible squamous differentiation markers (PKP1, DSC1, KRTAP19-8).
